slides.title: 10/10 things keeping you on your phone at night

slides.heading: scrolling _in the dark_
slides.top: lights off, _brightness all the way down_, the phone a hand away from your face
slides.text:
the room disappears, so the feed is _the only thing left_ to look at

nothing in the dark tells you it's late, so _it never feels late_

slides.heading: checking the time _at 3am_
slides.top: you wake up, grab the phone to see the time, and _the notifications are right under it_
slides.text:
one glance turns into _forty minutes_

and a bright screen at arm's length is _a bad way to drift back off_
slides.bottom: you were asleep. now you're _awake and informed_

slides.heading: _"after this one"_
slides.text:
every video is short, so stopping always feels _30 seconds away_

the feed never ends, so _you have to end it_, at the moment you're most tired

i struggled with this for years until i built something that _puts my apps to sleep at bedtime_

slides.heading: no _ending_ to the day
slides.top: no dinner time, no lights out, no one telling you to go to bed anymore
slides.text:
so the day ends _whenever your phone lets go_

which is usually _when it dies_

slides.heading: charging it _next to your pillow_
slides.text:
a phone that can't die is a night that _can't end_

and it's the first thing you touch in the morning, _before your feet hit the floor_
slides.bottom: give the night an ending before you need willpower to find one
